mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 4.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero in these episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which raises real discount rates and erodes real earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12-mo avg AND CPIAUCSL > 12-mo avg in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both proxies exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 6-month moving average by more than 10% signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports broader equities, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in more than 40% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) in the same month signals a mixed labor market where job creation is insufficient to absorb new entrants, leading to muted wage growth and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both proxies move in this direction simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month average for four consecutive months signals reduced household buffer capacity, which increases reliance on credit and consumer spending, supporting corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-mo average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive in more than 50% of triggered periods.
